_comment: Optional user personalization for the Soniox engines. Copy this file to 'personal_settings.json' and customize the vocabulary block. If 'personal_settings.json' is absent, SONIOX_CONTEXT stays None and no personalization is sent. The whole vocabulary block — the 'terms' list, the 'general' domain/topic block, and the 'text' section — is used by every Soniox engine (Soniox Live and the async upload slot) uniformly. 'text' is a free-form background passage that lets the model disambiguate a term from sentence context — useful when a name sounds like a common word and a bare term does not reliably win (see https://soniox.com/docs/stt/concepts/context). The whole context (general + terms + text together) shares an 8,000-token limit (~10,000 characters). The Groq APIs ignore this file entirely.

general.value: Your main topics here (e.g. software development, academic writing, specific field)

terms: Technical term the model often misrecognizes
Foreign word commonly used in your dictation
vocabulary.text: Free-form background about your world, in any language (a short glossary, a project description, a few sentences). Its main value is disambiguation: a term listed above does not reliably beat a same-sounding everyday word, so a sentence of context tips the model the right way. Example: when a product or project name sounds like a common word, write 'X is the name of my software; when I dictate it I mean the product, not the ordinary word it sounds like.' Replace this with your own background, or drop the key if you don't need it.

push_to_talk._comment: Opt-in push-to-talk (Issue #66): tap the trigger key, release, then press-and-HOLD it; recording runs while held, releasing inserts the transcript. DEFAULT OFF -- switch it on in the settings app (Hotkeys tab), or set enabled to true here (the gesture then reads every trigger press). On German QWERTZ, AltGr (Ctrl+Alt) is filtered out, so typing @ \ { } [ ] | euro ~ never triggers it. trigger: lctrl (default, bottom-left) | rctrl (AltGr-safe) | lalt. insert: clipboard (default, paste like Ctrl+Alt+A) | type (fallback, simulated typing like Ctrl+Alt+H, for apps that block paste) | send | no_insert. The three thresholds are seconds (positive numbers): tap_window_s = first release to second press, min_hold_s = how long the second press is held before recording starts, release_tail_s = extra time kept after release so word-ends are not clipped.

soniox_endpointing._comment: OPTIONAL, OFF BY DEFAULT (Issue #121). Fine-tunes Soniox v5 real-time endpoint detection for the Soniox Live path only (the async upload path has no endpointing). With no keys here, nothing is sent and Soniox uses its own defaults -- behavior is unchanged. To tune, add any of: 'endpoint_sensitivity' (number -1.0..1.0, default 0.0; lower waits longer before ending a sentence -- Soniox documents -0.3 for dictation and slow speakers), 'endpoint_latency_adjustment_level' (integer 0..3, default 0; higher ends sentences sooner -- leave at 0 when using a negative sensitivity), 'max_endpoint_delay_ms' (number 500..3000, default 2000; hard cap on the wait after speech stops). Out-of-range or wrong-typed values are ignored with a warning and never sent. Concrete tuning is still being decided (follow-up issue).

hotkeys._comment: OPTIONAL (Issue #55). A PARTIAL override of the default hotkeys, keyed by action name -- config.py keeps the defaults; a listed action replaces its combo, unlisted actions keep theirs. Valid action names: start_recording, stop_recording_keyboard, stop_recording_clipboard, stop_recording_send, stop_recording_no_insert, retry_last_failed, cancel_recording, test_transcription, switch_api, open_history, open_settings, exit_program. A value is a combo string (e.g. "ctrl+alt+p") or, only for cancel_recording and exit_program (whose defaults are already lists), a list of combos. Modifiers: ctrl/control, alt, shift, win/windows. Keys: letters, digits, and F-keys f1-f24 -- including modifier-less ones like "f9". Avoid special characters like '#' and non-ASCII letters -- they can be typed into some apps, and having no fixed key code they are resolved against your active keyboard layout at startup, so every shipped default is a plain letter, digit or F-key. The umlaut key ('ue' or the literal umlaut) is the one accepted exception if you want it; like every action, it may be rebound. An unknown action, an unparseable combo, or a combo that would collide with another action is ignored with a warning in thoughtborne.log and that action's default stays -- the tool never fails to start over a bad hotkey. To use, add entries beside this comment, e.g.  "start_recording": "f9",  "exit_program": ["ctrl+alt+4", "ctrl+alt+q"].

defaults._comment: OPTIONAL (Issue #55). 'api' picks the transcription engine active at startup instead of the built-in default (soniox-live). Must be one of: soniox-live, soniox, groq-large, groq; anything else is ignored with a warning and the built-in default stays. Setting 'api' also outranks the engine the tool remembers from your last Ctrl+Alt+L switch (kept in its own runtime_state.json) — an explicit choice here wins, and without it the remembered engine is used. Example:  "api": "groq-large". (A dictation-language override is deliberately not offered yet -- it fans out into several engine-specific settings and needs its own design.)

ui._comment: GUI-only (Issue #144). The graphical settings app remembers its own display language here — 'language' is 'de' or 'en'. The dictation tool itself ignores this whole block; it has no effect on transcription, hotkeys, or the console. If absent, the settings app starts in English — a stored value here is the only thing that overrides that default. Example:  "language": "de".
